claims.text: ICRC: Art 79 AP I — journalists are civilians and must be respected and protected; lose protection 'only if, and for such time as, they directly participate in hostilities'; reporting or opinion does not make a journalist a target; media facilities generally civilian objects; customary rule 34 applies in non-international conflicts.

CPJ 14 Aug 2024 urged Israel to stop labelling killed journalists terrorists without proof; listed earlier cases (Murtaja 2018, Salama and al-Kumi 2012, Shihab 2014, Abu Halima 2004); Irene Khan: accusations appear to be 'a licence to kill journalists'; de la Serna: 'Smear campaigns endanger journalists and erode public trust in the media.'

+972 (Aug 2025), from three intelligence sources: a 'Legitimization Cell' set up after Oct 7 to find intelligence linking journalists to militancy, to counter criticism and protect international (US arms) support; 'a push to find one journalist who might not be so innocent'; no IDF response in the report.

IDF (Feb 2025): 'The IDF has never, and will never, deliberately target journalists'; takes all feasible measures; names Thuraya (Hamas squad deputy commander per a document), Hamza Dahdouh (PIJ operative 'disguised' as a journalist), Ismail Abu Omar (filmed himself at Nir Oz on Oct 7), al-Ghoul; says it 'cannot disclose the intelligence' without revealing sources; Hamas embeds in civilian sites.
Oct 2023 IDF letter to Reuters and AFP: 'we cannot guarantee your employees' safety'; Hamas operating 'in the vicinity of journalists and civilians'.
